newsitem.title: USA: Philadelphia Fed says local economy slowed in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Philadelphia Fed says local economy slowed in Q2.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia said the economy in the third U.S. economic district slowed "significantly" in the second quarter from a robust pace of growth in the first three months of the year.
"The third district economy slowed significantly in the second quarter, after robust growth in the first," the Philadelphia Fed said in its Regional Highlights report for the second quarter.
The nation's third economic distric encompasses Delaware, the eastern region of Pennsylvania and the southern portion of New Jersey.
Turning to the jobs market, the Philadelphia Fed said there was "essentially no job growth" in the region in the second quarter.
The report said payroll job growth in the tri-state area expanded by 0.1 percent in the second quarter against a strong 0.9 percent increase in the first three months of the year.

"The slowdown in tri-state employment growth stands in contrast to the national economy, which posted identical employment increases of 0.6 percent in the first and second quarters," the Philadelphia Fed report said.
The region's estimated unemployment rate for the second quarter was at 5.2 percent.
The Regional Highlights paper also said that given the economic slowdown in the second quarter, there was "little reason to expect an increase in inflation in the region any time soon."
The report said residential and non-residential construction continued to exceed 1996 levels, but noted both were weakening. Housing permists, it added, were declining.
The report said local retail sales growth was modest, while banking lending was up slightly.
